message.content:
**Answer:** One of the most iconic and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser)** by **Auguste Rodin**, completed in 1889. It exemplifies the era’s shift toward expressive realism and has become a symbol of romantic love in art history. --- ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin (1840–1917) | | **Year Completed** | 1889 | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist influence; dynamic, emotive form | | **Material** | Bronze (originally cast in 1889; many editions exist) | | **Cultural Impact** | • Became a staple of 19th‑century sculpture collections worldwide.
• Influenced later modernist approaches to form and emotion.
• Frequently reproduced in prints, postcards, and popular media. | --- ### Contextualizing within the 19th‑Century Sculpture Landscape - **Other major works of the era**: - *The Gates of Hell* (unfinished, 1880–1908) – a monumental project by Rodin. - *The Thinker* (1902–1904) – although technically early 20th, it was conceived during Rodin’s late 19th‑century period and reflects the same stylistic concerns. - *The Birth of Venus* (by various artists, but the most famous 19th‑century version is by Alexandre Cabanel, 1863). - **Why “The Kiss” is often singled out**: - It captures the emotional intensity and naturalism that defined the latter half of the 19th century. - Its widespread reproduction and presence in major museums (e.g., Musée Rodin in Paris, the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York) cement its status as a cultural touchstone. --- ### Quick Reference | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Material | Current Location (Notable) | |-----------|--------|------|----------|----------------------------| | **The Kiss** | Auguste Rodin | 1889 | Bronze | Musée Rodin (Paris), Metropolitan Museum of Art (NY) | | **The Thinker** | Auguste Rodin | 1902–1904 | Bronze | Musée Rodin (Paris), Musée d’Orsay (Paris) | | **The Gates of Hell** | Auguste Rodin | 1880–1908 | Bronze | Musée Rodin (Paris) | | **The Birth of Venus** | Alexandre Cabanel | 1863 | Oil on canvas (not a sculpture) | Musée du Louvre (Paris) | --- **Bottom line:** While many masterpieces were produced in the 19th century, **Rodin’s “The Kiss”** is frequently regarded as the most emblematic and widely celebrated sculpture of that era.
